name: gateway_down
title: The router stops responding
description: Nothing past it can be reached or measured. The agent has to say so without inventing conclusions about layers it can no longer see.

card.title: The far end is slow to answer
card.summary: Your router and the path out to the internet both look normal, but the services we test are taking 98 ms to send their first byte, about 79 ms more than the network itself explains.
remediation: Check whether other sites are fine; if they are, the problem is at the far end and not with your connection.
Check the service's own status page.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

evidence.label: name resolution phase of the synthetic request

card.title: This device looks like the problem
card.summary: The signals that changed are on this machine rather than on the network around it: CPU 29%, 0.9% of connections retransmitted.
remediation: Close whatever is using the most CPU or bandwidth on this device.
Restart this device's network adapter.
Check for an update to this device's network adapter driver.

evidence.label: system-wide CPU utilisation
TCP segment retransmissions divided by segments sent
receive drops divided by receive packets over the interval
transmit drops divided by transmit packets over the interval

card.title: Congestion past your router
card.summary: Your own network looks fine: your router answers in 4 ms. Past it, the path out is adding about 16 ms. That points to your internet connection or your provider rather than anything in your home.
remediation: Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.
If this keeps happening, export a diagnostic bundle and send it to your internet provider.
Plug in an ethernet cable for anything important in the next few minutes.

card.title: Your router is slow to respond
card.summary: Round trips to your own router are taking 6 ms with 1 ms of variation. On a healthy home network this is a couple of milliseconds and steady, so something local is loading it up.
remediation: Check whether something on your network is saturating the connection, such as a large upload or a backup.
Power cycle your router: unplug it for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.
Plug in an ethernet cable for anything important in the next few minutes.

evidence.label: fraction of gateway probes with no reply
mean absolute deviation of gateway RTT within the probe burst
round trip time to the default gateway

card.title: Your router is slow to respond
card.summary: Round trips to your own router are taking 3 ms with 1 ms of variation. On a healthy home network this is a couple of milliseconds and steady, so something local is loading it up.
remediation: Check whether something on your network is saturating the connection, such as a large upload or a backup.
Power cycle your router: unplug it for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.
Plug in an ethernet cable for anything important in the next few minutes.
